html:
The Kitselas, "people of the canyon", are one of the fourteen tribes of the Tsimshian nation of northwestern British Columbia. Their villages stood at Kitselas Canyon on the Skeena River, east of today's Terrace.

The canyon was a narrow, dangerous stretch of river and a key point on the trade route between the coast and the interior. By holding it, the Kitselas could control and tax the traffic between the coastal Tsimshian and the inland Gitxsan. Their villages had rows of cedar houses and carved poles, like those of the Haida. Kitselas Canyon is now a National Historic Site of Canada, with replica longhouses and poles.
